_comment: Data-driven REWARDED-AD HOOK config for Defenders of the Realm / Echoes of Elarion. Drives the thin AdGateService interpreter (WORK_ORDER_ad_generator.md sec.A). Owner data-first style: WHERE/WHEN an ad offer appears + WHAT it grants is DATA here, not hardcoded branches. The existing RewardedAdManager (Assets/_Modules/Village/Monetization/RewardedAdManager.cs) is the SDK seam (ShowAdInternal); this file replaces its single fixed 480s cooldown + implicit reward with a placement/reward TABLE.
_status: SPEC, NOT LIVE CONFIG (verified 2026-08-07): no AdGateService exists and NOTHING under Assets/**.cs reads this file. It describes intent for an interpreter that has not been written. Kept and corrected rather than deleted because the WO-912 rulings below are binding the moment it IS wired, and a stale spec is how a retired placement comes back.

_sources.sdkSeam: Assets/_Modules/Village/Monetization/RewardedAdManager.cs (ShowAdInternal stub); the provider-agnostic seam is DeNelle.Core.Ads.IAdService
_sources.covenant: docs/monetization-v2-spec.md sec.5.3 - convenience is TIME-SAVING only, never combat-power; the same covenant binds ad rewards
_sources.rulings: WORK_ORDER_912_ad_revenue_free_path.md sec.9 (owner ruled D1/D2/D4/D5/D7/D8 on 2026-08-07) + sec.9.3 (the policy shield)

_schema.placement: { id (string, unique, stable key the call-site passes), enabled (bool), surface (enum: store|harvest|build|defeat|daily|tree), rewardId (FK->rewards[].id), cooldownSeconds (int, per-placement; overrides global), dailyCap (int, max grants/placement/local-day, 0=unlimited), requiresFlag (FeatureFlags name or empty), prompt { headline, body, cta } (localizable strings shown on the offer button/modal), priority (int, higher wins when two placements compete for one surface) }
_schema.reward: { id (string, unique), kind (enum: currency|timeskip|harvest|buff|cosmeticTrial), grant (object shaped by kind), description (string, player-facing), maxStack (int, how many unclaimed grants may queue, 0=apply-immediately) }
_schema.global: { defaultCooldownSeconds, hardDailyCap (sum across ALL placements), adProvider (stub|unityads|levelplay), respectDoNotSell (bool) }

_LAW_1_NO_PREMIUM_CURRENCY: ★ NO AD REWARD MAY EVER GRANT CRYSTALS, OR ANY CURRENCY BOUGHT WITH REAL MONEY. ★ This is not a balance preference, it is the thing that keeps the ad account alive. WO-912 sec.9.3: AdMob forbids rewards 'directly convertible into direct monetary items' and Unity forbids incentivising with 'anything of value'; our reward passes ONLY because minutes off a build timer cannot be transferred, traded, sold or cashed out. Crystals are the SKR on-ramp - the moment an ad pays them out, the reward becomes arguably convertible and the policy protection evaporates along with the covenant. Enforced by AdPlacementCovenantRegression case [no-premium-grant], which is a HARD FAIL, not a warning.
_LAW_2_TIMESKIP_HAS_ONE_AUTHORITY: The timeskip amount is BuildTimerConfig.adSkipSeconds (Assets/_Modules/Core/Catalog/BuildTimerConfig.cs:92, currently 600s = 10 min). The number below is a MIRROR for the spec's readability and is pinned equal to it by regression. Change the config, never this file alone - a second copy of a number is how the two drift and nobody notices.
_LAW_3_AD_UNIT_IDS: Every enabled placement carries the LevelPlay adUnitId it maps to. These are NOT secrets - they ship inside the APK and are visible to anyone who unpacks it - but they ARE the join between a dashboard and this repo, and an unrecorded join is one that drifts the first time somebody creates a unit and forgets to tell anyone. Recorded here so the mapping is reviewable in a diff. Per owner ruling D5 remote config (Neon + the existing api/ rail) may OVERRIDE these at runtime, so a unit can be swapped without shipping a build; these are the defaults and the record, not a hardcode. Pinned by AdPlacementCovenantRegression case [ad-unit-mapped].

global.covenantLine: Ads are always optional. You are never required to watch one. Ever.
global._hardDailyCapNote: 14 = the SUM of the three enabled placements' own caps (build 10 + harvest 3 + daily 1), so each placement's cap is what binds and none starves the others. It went 12 -> 10 when build.skip was the only placement, then -> 14 when the owner re-enabled harvest and daily on 2026-08-07. IF A GLOBAL BRAKE IS WANTED it must be a deliberate number BELOW the sum, and it should be the owner's, not a default: set below 14 and the placements start competing by priority, which is a product decision about which offer a player sees last.

rewards._note: REPLACES reward.build.skip1, which granted { kind: 'instant-build', count: 1 } - a FULL completion. That contradicted the design WO-912 is built on: the near-miss math in D1 (a ~2h build needing 10 watches and still finishing 20 min short) only works if a watch buys MINUTES. An instant finish also hands away for free exactly what crystals are sold for. Non-convertible either way, so the policy shield held - but the economy did not. seconds MUST equal BuildTimerConfig.adSkipSeconds; see _LAW_2.

UNREACHABLE IN V1 - no enabled placement references it. Kept as vocabulary. Coins are a SOFT currency with no purchase path, so it does not trip _LAW_1; it is parked by D4 (ads stay on queue timers for V1), not by policy.

rewards._REMOVED_2026_08_19_reward_glimmer_trick: DELETED (owner ruling 2026-08-19). It granted 15 glimmer and was an ORPHAN - no placement referenced it - but _LAW_1 bans an ad reward paying any currency BOUGHT WITH REAL MONEY, and glimmer is still sold in packs.json today (glimmer=300, glimmer=400, a bundle with glimmer:1000). Its own _note called it safe because 'glimmer buys cosmetics only', which was true of the SPEND side and silent about the SELL side. Wiring any placement to it would have shipped a policy violation past a guard that may not list glimmer as premium. Owner: 'we removed glimmer long time ago', 'we use crystals' - the wider retirement is WO-1126, which is blocked on a ruling because it touches three months of real player balances. This one line needed no ruling: an orphan on the banned side of LAW 1 is pure downside.

rewards._note: LIVE (owner reversed D4 on 2026-08-07). Legal under _LAW_1 by construction: it grants a RATE for a duration, not a currency, so there is nothing here that could be converted to money.

REPLACES the deleted reward.daily.bonusChest, which paid 500 coins AND +100 CRYSTALS nested in a 'bonus' object. The coin half is kept at its full original value so the chest still reads as a chest; the crystal half is gone permanently under _LAW_1 and is NOT a scope decision that can be reversed - it is the difference between a reward with no path to money and one with a path to money. Coins are a soft currency with no purchase route, so 500 of them is not a policy problem at any amount.

_REMOVED_2026_08_07.reward.crystals.small: DELETED. +150 crystals. Violated _LAW_1 outright - it paid the SKR on-ramp currency for watching an ad, which is precisely the convertibility AdMob and Unity prohibit. It was ENABLED in this file while WO-912 was preparing to tell Unity in writing that no ad reward can reach money. Never re-add.
_REMOVED_2026_08_07.reward.daily.bonusChest: DELETED. +500 coins AND +100 crystals. Same violation, hidden in a 'bonus' sub-object - which is exactly why the regression walks grants RECURSIVELY rather than checking the top-level currency field.
_REMOVED_2026_08_07.reward.revive.freeContinue: DELETED. Retired with its placement by owner ruling D7 (2026-08-07): a battle-continue is COMBAT POWER, and the covenant is convenience-only. This is the one deletion that is about the game rather than the ad network.
_REMOVED_2026_08_07.place.defeat.continue: DELETED. Owner ruling D7 - retire. It also carried requiresFlag 'overworldencounter', so it would have armed itself the moment that flag went on.

placements._adUnitNameNote: THE ONE INCONSISTENT NAME. The other two units are named after their placement id; this one follows a <format>_<purpose>_<platform> convention I suggested before checking what the game already called the placement. Matching the placement id is better - it gives 1:1 attribution between LevelPlay revenue and our telemetry with no mapping table to drift - so this unit should be renamed to 'place.build.skip' in the dashboard. Renaming does NOT change the adUnitId, so nothing here needs editing when it happens; delete this note instead.

prompt.headline: Speed It Up
prompt.body: Watch a short clip to take 10 minutes off this job.

placements._note: THE ONLY V1 PLACEMENT (owner rulings D4 + D7, 2026-08-07). Copy changed from 'Finish Now' / 'Skip this build instantly' because that promised an instant completion the reward no longer grants - and 'Finish Now' is the CRYSTAL button's name (WO-898). Two different things must not share a label. requiresFlag added: this was empty, so a wired interpreter would have offered ads while ff.rewardedadskip was OFF and every other path refuses them. cooldown 300 -> 480 to match RewardedAdManager.CooldownSeconds; dailyCap 5 -> 10 to match the ruled window.

prompt.headline: Double Your Harvest
prompt.body: The echoes work twice as fast for an hour.

placements._note: ENABLED 2026-08-07 - owner REVERSED D4 ("can you do harvest doubler, its simple and im the only tester so its good"). Legal under _LAW_1: the grant is a rate multiplier for a duration, not a currency. Note this is the ONE placement whose reward can stack with itself over time (maxStack 1), so its 3600s cooldown is doing real work - do not shorten it without re-checking the offline-harvest economy.

prompt.headline: Daily Bonus
prompt.body: Claim today's bonus - one free watch a day.

placements._note: ENABLED 2026-08-07 - owner reversed D4 alongside the harvest doubler. Points at reward.daily.chest (500 coins), NOT the deleted reward.daily.bonusChest (500 coins + 100 CRYSTALS). Enabling the placement was the owner's scope call; dropping the crystals was not a scope call and is not reversible - see _LAW_1. dailyCap 1 + cooldown 0 is correct here: the cap IS the gate for a once-a-day claim.
